title: Simultaneous finite-stage realization of bounds and heart witnesses
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed poset [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\mathcal C_i$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category] with bounded t-structures [def-weil-t-structure]. Supply exact t-exact functors $T_{j/i}$ for $i\le j$, literal identity functors $T_{i/i}=1$, and shift-compatible exact associators $a_{k,j,i}$ satisfying unit and pentagon. Form the additive pair category $P$ with objects $(i,K)$ and
$$\operatorname{Hom}_P((i,K),(j,L))=\varinjlim_{m\ge i,j}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_m}(T_{m/i}K,T_{m/j}L)$$
[def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups], with transport $u\mapsto a_{n,m,j}T_{n/m}(u)a_{n,m,i}^{-1}$ and composition at a common stage. Write $j_i:\mathcal C_i\to P$ for the inclusion and use its canonical identifications $j_mT_{m/i}\cong j_i$. Assume that every finite diagram of morphisms and asserted equalities in $P$ is realized at one stage, with equalities holding after further enlargement.

Fix $Z=(i,K)$ and finitely many given isomorphisms $e_s:Z\cong j_{i_s}A_s$ in $P$. For each $s$ prescribe a condition $A_s\in\mathcal C_{i_s}^{\le b_s}$ or $A_s\in\mathcal C_{i_s}^{\ge a_s}$, where $a_s,b_s\in\mathbf Z$. There is one $m\ge i,i_s$ and actual isomorphisms $T_{m/i}K\cong T_{m/i_s}A_s$ representing all the given $e_s$ and their inverses, such that $T_{m/i}K$ satisfies every prescribed bound simultaneously.

In particular, if $Z$ belongs to both isomorphism closures $P^{\le0}$ and $P^{\ge0}$ of the finite-stage halves, then some $m\ge i$ satisfies $T_{m/i}K\in\mathcal C_m^{\le0}\cap\mathcal C_m^{\ge0}$. There are isomorphisms in $\mathcal C_m$ and $P$, respectively,
$$T_{m/i}K\cong H_m^0(T_{m/i}K),\qquad Z\cong j_mH_m^0(T_{m/i}K),$$
where $H_m^0=\tau_m^{\ge0}\tau_m^{\le0}$ [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. Thus $P^{\le0}\cap P^{\ge0}$ is exactly the isomorphism closure of finite-stage hearts. Neither faithfulness of $j_i$ nor reflection of bounds by the transition functors is assumed.

proof.text: For each $s$ put $f_s=e_s$ and $g_s=e_s^{-1}$. Apply the assumed finite-diagram realization to these arrows and to the finitely many equations $g_sf_s=1_Z$, $f_sg_s=1_{j_{i_s}A_s}$. It supplies a common stage, and after the allowed further enlargement a single $m\ge i,i_s$ with arrows $u_s:T_{m/i}K\to T_{m/i_s}A_s$ and $v_s$ in the reverse direction satisfying $v_su_s=1$ and $u_sv_s=1$. Thus $(u_s,v_s)$ is an actual isomorphism representing the specified $e_s$ and its specified inverse under the canonical identifications with $P$. For an empty witness family take $m=i$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1), pp. 61–62: agent-written abstract finite-stage argument, using the finite-diagram realization hypothesis explicitly supplied in this item

proof.text: Write $X=T_{m/i}K$. By t-exactness, an upper bound $A_s\in\mathcal C_{i_s}^{\le b_s}$ gives $T_{m/i_s}A_s\in\mathcal C_m^{\le b_s}$; a lower bound gives $T_{m/i_s}A_s\in\mathcal C_m^{\ge a_s}$. The halves are strictly full by [def-weil-t-structure], also after shifts, so the isomorphism $u_s$ puts $X$ in that same half. This holds for every $s$ at this one $m$, proving the simultaneous bounds.

proof.text: If $Z\in P^{\le0}\cap P^{\ge0}$, the definitions of the two isomorphism closures give one upper witness $A_+$ and one lower witness $A_-$, each isomorphic to $Z$. Apply steps 1–2 to this two-element family with bounds zero. They give $X=T_{m/i}K\in\mathcal C_m^{\le0}\cap\mathcal C_m^{\ge0}$, the finite-stage heart by [def-weil-t-structure].

proof.text: Use the truncation adjunctions in clause (1) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. Since $X\in\mathcal C_m^{\le0}$, the counit $c:\tau_m^{\le0}X\to X$ is an isomorphism: the adjunction gives $h:X\to\tau_m^{\le0}X$ with $ch=1_X$, and injectivity of $\operatorname{Hom}(\tau_m^{\le0}X,\tau_m^{\le0}X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\tau_m^{\le0}X,X)$ gives $hc=1$. Dually the unit $X\to\tau_m^{\ge0}X$ is an isomorphism because $X\in\mathcal C_m^{\ge0}$. Hence $X\cong\tau_m^{\ge0}X\cong\tau_m^{\ge0}\tau_m^{\le0}X=H_m^0(X)$. Apply $j_m$ and compose with $Z\cong j_mX$ to obtain $Z\cong j_mH_m^0(X)$. This cohomology object is in the heart by the same clause. Conversely any $j_mB$ with $B$ in the finite-stage heart is in both half closures; the same holds for every object isomorphic to it. This proves the asserted equality of closures.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q77-0e437e7e3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and every step in full. No new nodes. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from the unsplit base (statement sha1 bae9b06966, the same as earlier snapshots); proof_deps equal the union of the step uses. Step 1: the item's finite-diagram realization hypothesis, applied to e_s, e_s^{-1} and both inverse equations and followed by one more enlargement, gives actual inverse pairs (u_s, v_s) at a single stage m. Identities in P are represented by literal identities (T(1)=1, unchanged by associator conjugation). The empty family takes m=i. Step 2: an exact t-exact functor keeps shifted bounds, and the strictly full halves of def-weil-t-structure move each bound along u_s. Upper and lower bounds are treated separately, with no reflection of bounds and no faithfulness. Step 3: applying steps 1-2 to the two half witnesses lands in the stage heart. Step 4: the adjunctions of lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles clause (1) (also in its blueprint_update) make the counit tau^{<=0}X->X an isomorphism (checked: ch=1, and c(hc)=c with the adjunction bijection gives hc=1), and dually the unit X->tau^{>=0}X. So X is isomorphic to H^0_m(X) and Z to j_m H^0_m(X); the converse inclusion is immediate. Edge cases checked: empty family, the zero object, incompatible bounds, a one-point I. Source checked: Bhatt-Scholze Prop 6.8.14(1), pp. 61-62, only an equivalence of constructible categories, so proof_origin=agent is correct; BBD 1.3.3 comes through the cited node; no SGA. The parent lem-per-adic-common-stage-truncations cites the item's statement for exactly this heart passage.
